memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and migraine.
Evidence: Symptoms of retrosternal burning after meals, occasional nausea, and throbbing unilateral headaches with photophobia.
Symptoms and examination: Patient reports heartburn 3-4 times weekly, relieved by antacid; headaches 2 days per month, moderate intensity; abdomen soft, no tenderness; neurological exam normal.
Inhaler: No inhaler prescribed. Technique checked: not applicable.
Smoking status: former, stopped 2020, pack-years 20.
Plan: Start pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals, antacid gel SOS; start propranolol 40 mg OD for migraine prophylaxis, topiramate 25 mg HS, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, naproxen 500 mg SOS.

memories.text: I’ve noticed heartburn returns after eating spicy food or late nights, about twice a week. My migraines have been rare, just one mild episode last month that I treated with sumatriptan. I’m otherwise feeling fine and managing my cab shifts.

memories.text:
Diagnosis: Gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease, migraine.
Evidence: Increased heartburn symptoms, migraine well controlled.
Symptoms and examination: Heartburn 4‑5 times weekly, moderate, occasional regurgitation; headaches absent for 2 months; abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness; neurological exam normal.
Inhaler: No inhaler prescribed. Technique checked: not applicable.
Smoking status: former, stopped 2020, pack-years 20.
Plan: Increase pantoprazole to 40 mg BD, continue domperidone OD, arrange upper GI endoscopy to rule out erosive disease; maintain migraine prophylaxis.
